CPA-firm use case · 17 slides

Customer Onboarding Chatbot

Guide new clients from their first question to completed onboarding—with connected systems and clear staff responsibilities.

Explore the slides

Build the journey around trusted knowledge

The presentation starts with three foundations: approved FAQs, service-specific checklists and a defined customer journey. It shows how an assistant can combine intent recognition, stage tracking and system integrations to guide clients through onboarding.

The design separates conversational guidance from sensitive transactions. Payment and upload flows stay in dedicated systems, while staff retain responsibility for professional advice, exceptions and final document review.

The six-stage journey

StageAssistant role in the proposed design
Capture leadRecord contact details and service needs
RegisterGuide client details into the portal
EstimatePrepare a scope-based estimate for confirmation
PaymentSend a secure provider link and read status
UploadProvide checklists and track missing documents
VerifyFlag document issues for staff review and sign-off

Why Automate Onboarding?

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Customer Onboarding Chatbot T H E O P P O R T U N I T Y Why automate client onboarding? Today's pain points The same questions, every day Fees, deadlines, what to send, how to upload Missing documents Back-and-forth emails to chase incomplete files Leads arrive after hours Prospects asking at night wait until morning, or go elsewhere Manual data entry Staff retype client details into several systems What the bot should achieve • Answer common questions instantly, 24/7 • Guide each client to the next step • Collect details and documents once, securely • Hand complex questions to the right person • Free staff time for advisory work 2

Six-Stage Onboarding Journey

Customer Onboarding Chatbot 0 1 · J O U R N E Y The onboarding journey in six stages 1 Capture lead BOT Captures name, contact and need; answers first questions STAFF Calls back hot leads 2 Register BOT Collects client details into the portal STAFF Checks for conflicts of interest 3 Estimate BOT Gathers scope; shares an estimate from the price list STAFF Approves non-standard quotes 4 Take payment BOT Sends a secure payment link; confirms receipt STAFF Handles refunds and disputes 5 Upload documents BOT Sends the checklist; tracks what's missing; sends reminders STAFF Answers unusual document questions 6 Verify documents BOT Runs automatic checks on each file STAFF Reviews and signs off 4

Prepare the Knowledge

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Customer Onboarding Chatbot 0 2 · C O N V E R S AT I O N Prepare the knowledge first Checklists What each service needs from the client • Prior-year return • Profit and loss, balance sheet • Payroll reports, W-2s and 1099s • Owner ID and EIN letter Business tax return (example) FAQ Approved answers to common questions • What are your fees? • What are the deadlines? • How do I upload securely? • How long does it take? Reviewed by a partner Customer journey The stages, and what moves a client to the next one • Entry and exit for each stage • Who owns each step • Reminders and timings • When to involve staff The bot's flowchart The bot is only as good as these three documents. Write them with the team that does onboarding today, and keep them current each tax season. 6

Find the Client’s Stage

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Customer Onboarding Chatbot 0 2 · C O N V E R S AT I O N Find the client's stage, then respond Known contact? yes no Capture lead details Registered? yes no Start registration Estimate accepted? yes no Share or explain the estimate Paid? yes no Send the payment link All documents in? yes no Send the checklist of what's missing Documents verified? no Report status; staff review How it works • The stage comes from your systems (CRM, portal, payments), not from what the client says • The bot answers the client's question first, then nudges the next step • Clients can ask anything at any stage; the flowchart sets the default next step • When every check is “yes”, onboarding is complete and the engagement team takes over 8

Upload and Verification

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Customer Onboarding Chatbot 0 3 · A R C H I T E C T U R E Document upload and verification Request Bot sends the checklist and a secure upload link Upload Client uploads in the portal, not the chat Auto-check File type, readable, right form, right year, names match Chase Bot lists what's missing and sends reminders Staff review A preparer reviews flagged items and signs off Confirmed Client is told onboarding is complete Rules: documents never pass through the chat; automatic checks only flag issues and never reject a file on their own; a person signs off before onboarding is marked complete. 12

Security and Privacy in the Source Deck

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Customer Onboarding Chatbot 0 4 · T R U S T Security, privacy and compliance for a CPA firm Verify identity Sign-in through the client portal before showing any client-specific information. No sensitive data in chat SSNs, bank and card details go only to the secure portal or payment provider. Security plan (WISP) Tax preparers must keep a written information security plan; include the bot in it. Client consent (Sec. 7216) Using or disclosing tax return information, including to AI vendors, may need client consent. Vendor terms No training on client data; limited retention; a confidentiality agreement. Audit and retention Log conversations and actions; delete on a set schedule. Not legal advice: confirm requirements with your counsel. 13

Human Handoff

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Customer Onboarding Chatbot 0 4 · T R U S T When the bot hands off to a person Hand off when the client… Asks for tax advice: “Should I become an S-corp?” goes to a CPA Questions or negotiates fees: Non-standard pricing needs a partner Is upset or complains: A person responds, quickly Is stuck: Two failed attempts at the same step Asks for a person: Always honour it The bot informs; people advise • Shares facts from approved FAQs and checklists only • Never gives tax, legal or investment advice • Says clearly that it is an AI assistant • Passes the conversation summary to staff, so the client doesn't repeat themselves • Tells the client who will follow up, and when 14

Key Takeaways

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Key takeaways 1 Write the checklist, FAQ and journey first: they are the bot's knowledge. 2 Understand intent and entities, find the client's stage, then guide the next step. 3 Integrate with CRM, portal, payments and documents, with least-privilege access. 4 Keep sensitive data out of chat, follow WISP and Section 7216 rules, and inform, not advise. 5 Roll out in phases and measure each stage of the funnel. 17

Frequently asked questions

What are the six onboarding stages?

The presentation follows lead capture, registration, estimate, payment, document upload and document verification.

How does the assistant choose the next step?

It identifies intent and relevant details, checks the client’s stage in the CRM, portal and payment systems, answers the immediate question and guides the next onboarding step.

Where are payments and documents handled?

In the proposed design, payments use a payment-provider link and documents are uploaded through a secure portal. The chatbot reads status rather than collecting card details or receiving documents in chat.

Who makes the final document-verification decision?

Automatic checks flag issues; staff review and sign off before onboarding is marked complete. The deck does not propose automatic rejection of files by the bot.

When should the assistant hand off?

The deck routes requests for professional advice, non-standard fees, complaints, repeated difficulties and explicit requests for a person to staff.

How is success measured?

Suggested measures include onboarding time, lead conversion, first-time document completeness, staff time saved, questions resolved and client satisfaction.
